sourceEvidence.label: Plainsong sidecar signing and release-trust boundary

assessment.summary: The Rust sidecar inherits Electron-only execution privileges. A per-binary entitlement policy is the proportionate launch fix, with service isolation deferred unless new evidence justifies it.

nonNegotiables: Preserve packaged dictation and meeting capture.
Reject privilege drift in the exact app and ZIP.
Do not add a process hop to the dictation hot path without measured evidence.
assumptions: The native Rust sidecar does not require Electron JIT, unsigned executable memory, disabled library validation, or Apple Events.
Whether the sidecar requires a microphone entitlement must be settled by packaged capture testing.

opportunities.title: Give the Rust sidecar a dedicated least-privilege signing policy
opportunities.summary: Route the sidecar through a specialized entitlement file and make the release trust gate reject forbidden privileges.
opportunities.diagnosis: The signing callback specializes two native helpers but lets the Rust sidecar inherit the Electron child policy.

evidence.claim: The inherited policy grants JIT, unsigned executable memory, disabled library validation, microphone, and Apple Events.
The baseline release gate did not reject broad sidecar privileges.
The packaged sidecar carries the inherited broad entitlement set.
The existing per-helper signing callback can own a dedicated sidecar policy without changing runtime IPC.

desiredInvariants: The Rust sidecar never carries Electron JIT or library-validation bypass privileges.
The Rust sidecar never carries Apple Events authority.
The sidecar carries microphone authority only when exact-package capture proves it is required.
The release gate rejects forbidden sidecar privileges in both the release app and the app extracted from the ZIP.

options.title: Per-binary entitlement override
options.summary: Give the sidecar its own entitlement file and enforce it in the release trust gate.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The sidecar no longer consumes the inherited policy.
The trust gate receives a sidecar-specific forbidden set.
A newly signed package must demonstrate an empty or explicitly minimal sidecar entitlement set.
The existing signing boundary is extended rather than replaced.

tradeoffs.assessment: The sidecar loses ambient execution and Apple Events authority, and future drift fails the release gate.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inspect exact-package entitlements and run every forbidden-entitlement regression.

tradeoffs.assessment: Signing policy changes do not add a runtime hop or allocation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare packaged dictation latency and first-sample timing with the existing baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: No process or retained runtime state is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the existing idle memory gate on the new package.

tradeoffs.assessment: Runtime behavior should be unchanged, but microphone or system-audio capture could depend on a privilege currently inherited accidentally.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run packaged microphone, system-audio, shortcut, and Speech QA before acceptance.

tradeoffs.assessment: The trust report names forbidden sidecar privileges directly.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review JSON and Markdown output for one passing and each failing fixture.

tradeoffs.assessment: The change is isolated to signing and verification and can be reverted without data migration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Build once with the dedicated policy and confirm no application data changes.

residualRisks: Exact-package capture may prove that a narrowly scoped audio entitlement is required.
The Electron main process retains broad privileges that must remain justified separately.

workPackages: Add the dedicated entitlement file and signing route.
Build and exercise the exact package.
acceptanceCriteria: The sidecar has no forbidden entitlement in the app or ZIP.
Packaged dictation, meeting audio, shortcuts, and Speech remain functional.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Remove the sidecar override and its trust check only if packaged evidence proves a required privilege, then replace the empty policy with the narrowest demonstrated entitlement rather than restoring the inherited set.

options.title: Isolated capability services
options.summary: Split capture, secrets, and privileged actions into independently sandboxed services with narrow protocols.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Isolation narrows authority, but current packaged binaries still require direct entitlement repair during migration.
The release gate still needs per-service privilege enforcement.
The current sidecar remains overprivileged until the migration is complete.
A new service boundary replaces rather than extends the current callback structure.

tradeoffs.assessment: Compromise containment could be stronger if each service receives a capability-limited protocol and entitlement set.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model the proposed protocols and validate each service against concrete attack paths.

tradeoffs.assessment: Additional process hops and serialization would enter latency-sensitive capture or transcription paths.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prototype the hot path and compare first-sample, p50, and p95 dictation latency.

tradeoffs.assessment: Multiple services require additional processes, runtimes, and buffers.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare idle and active resident memory with the current sidecar.

tradeoffs.assessment: Failure isolation improves, but lifecycle coordination and partial service failure become new risks.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise service crashes, restart, backpressure, and in-flight recovery.

tradeoffs.assessment: Packaging, signing, logging, crash diagnosis, and release verification expand for every service.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Build a release checklist and measure added artifact and diagnostic surface.

tradeoffs.assessment: The current JSON-RPC state owner would need staged extraction and compatibility support.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Design a dual-path migration and prove rollback while old and new services coexist.

residualRisks: Protocol validation defects can replace ambient-authority defects.
The current package remains vulnerable until migration finishes.

workPackages: Migrate and remove the monolithic sidecar authority.
acceptanceCriteria: Each service has a documented authority set and failure boundary.
Latency and memory remain within product budgets.
migrationNotes: Keep the per-binary entitlement fix throughout migration.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Retain the existing sidecar path behind a versioned protocol until service parity and package evidence are complete.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the per-binary entitlement override for launch. Reconsider service isolation only if later findings show that native sidecar compromise remains a high-impact recurring boundary.

openQuestions: Does exact-package microphone or system-audio capture require one narrowly scoped sidecar entitlement?
